question: In Joel 1:1-3, to whom did the word of the LORD come, and what generational transmission of this unprecedented crisis was commanded?
opt1: Joel the son of Pethuel; old men and inhabitants to tell their children, their children to tell their children, and their children another generation
opt2: Joel the son of Elkanah; priests to write the calamity upon bronze rolls to be read every sabbatical year
opt3: Joel the son of Azariah; kings of Judah to proclaim a national fast throughout all fenced cities
opt4: Joel the son of Shaphat; prophets to inscribe the vision upon the gates of the temple in Jerusalem
correct: Joel the son of Pethuel; old men and inhabitants to tell their children, their children to tell their children, and their children another generation
explanation: Joel 1:1, 3 (KJV) - "The word of the LORD that came to Joel the son of Pethuel ... Tell ye your children of it, and let your children tell their children, and their children another generation."

question: According to Joel 1:4, what fourfold successive wave of destructive insect swarms stripped the land of all vegetation?
opt1: That which the cankerworm left hath the locust eaten; that which the locust left hath the caterpillar eaten; and that which the caterpillar left hath the palmerworm eaten
opt2: That which the palmerworm left hath the locust eaten; that which the locust left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the cankerworm left hath the caterpiller eaten
opt3: That which the locust left hath the palmerworm eaten; that which the palmerworm left hath the hornet eaten; and that which the hornet left hath the worm consumed
opt4: That which the caterpillar left hath the cankerworm eaten; that which the cankerworm left hath the beetle eaten; and that which the beetle left hath the drought destroyed
correct: That which the palmerworm left hath the locust eaten; that which the locust left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the cankerworm left hath the caterpiller eaten
explanation: Joel 1:4 (KJV) - "That which the palmerworm hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the cankerworm left hath the caterpiller eaten."

question: In Joel 1:5-7, why are drunkards and wine-drinkers commanded to awake and weep, and how is the invading destructive nation described?
opt1: The vineyards of Samaria are burned with fire; for an army of horsemen from the north hath trampled the vats and slain the vinedressers
opt2: The storehouses of wine are plundered by Tyre; for the Philistines have broken down the fences and carried away the golden flagons
opt3: The new wine is cut off from their mouth; for a nation is come up upon the land, strong, and without number, whose teeth are the teeth of a lion, laying waste the vine and barking the fig tree clean bare
opt4: The grape harvest is spoiled by bitter drought; for the Assyrian host hath poisoned the springs and felled the orchards of Sharon
correct: The new wine is cut off from their mouth; for a nation is come up upon the land, strong, and without number, whose teeth are the teeth of a lion, laying waste the vine and barking the fig tree clean bare
explanation: Joel 1:5-7 (KJV) - "Awake, ye drunkards, and weep; and howl, all ye drinkers of wine, because of the new wine; for it is cut off from your mouth. For a nation is come up upon my land, strong, and without number, whose teeth are the teeth of a lion, and he hath the cheek teeth of a great lion. He hath laid my vine waste, and barked my fig tree: he hath made it clean bare, and cast it away; the branches thereof are made white."

question: According to Joel 1:8-9, like whom is the nation commanded to lament, and what cessation in temple worship caused the priests to mourn?
opt1: Lament like a mother bereaved of her only son; the morning and evening burnt offerings of bullocks have ceased
opt2: Lament like an exile weeping by the rivers of Babylon; the incense of sweet spices is no longer burned upon the golden altar
opt3: Lament like a widow mourning in the dust; the silver trumpets of the sanctuary have been silenced by famine
opt4: Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth; the meat offering and the drink offering is cut off from the house of the LORD
correct: Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth; the meat offering and the drink offering is cut off from the house of the LORD
explanation: Joel 1:8-9 (KJV) - "Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth. The meat offering and the drink offering is cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests, the LORD's ministers, mourn."

question: In Joel 1:10-12, why are the husbandmen ashamed and vinedressers howling, and what fruit trees are described as withered?
opt1: The wheat and barley harvest of the field is perished, the corn is wasted, new wine dried up, oil languisheth; the vine, fig tree, pomegranate, palm, and apple tree are withered, because joy is withered away from the sons of men
opt2: The olive crop is blighted with mildew and the flax ruined; the cedar, cypress, and myrtle trees have shed their leaves in mourning
opt3: The threshing floors are swept by whirlwind; the sycamore, terebinth, and almond trees have been devoured by wild boars
opt4: The summer fruits have rotted in the baskets; the willow, oak, and fir trees are consumed by scorching desert winds
correct: The wheat and barley harvest of the field is perished, the corn is wasted, new wine dried up, oil languisheth; the vine, fig tree, pomegranate, palm, and apple tree are withered, because joy is withered away from the sons of men
explanation: Joel 1:10-12 (KJV) - "The field is wasted, the land mourneth; for the corn is wasted: the new wine is dried up, the oil languisheth. Be ye ashamed, O ye husbandmen; howl, O ye vinedressers, for the wheat and for the barley; because the harvest of the field is perished. The vine is dried up, and the fig tree languisheth; the pomegranate tree, the palm tree also, and the apple tree, even all the trees of the field, are withered: because joy is withered away from the sons of men."

question: According to Joel 1:13-14, what solemn emergency fast and assembly are the priests and ministers of the altar commanded to convene?
opt1: Blow the silver trumpets, assemble thirty mighty men, and offer seven bullocks upon the altar of burnt offering
opt2: Gird yourselves, lament, howl, lie all night in sackcloth; sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all inhabitants into the house of the LORD, and cry unto the LORD
opt3: Rent your garments, put dust upon your heads, and march around the walls of Zion seven times in silence
opt4: Fast for forty days, wear garments of camel's hair, and pour out libations of bitter water at the temple gate
correct: Gird yourselves, lament, howl, lie all night in sackcloth; sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all inhabitants into the house of the LORD, and cry unto the LORD
explanation: Joel 1:13-14 (KJV) - "Gird yourselves, and lament, ye priests: howl, ye ministers of the altar: come, lie all night in sackcloth, ye ministers of my God: for the meat offering and the drink offering is withholden from the house of your God. Sanctify ye a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land into the house of the LORD your God, and cry unto the LORD,"

question: What solemn lamentation and characterization of the Day of the LORD is proclaimed in Joel 1:15?
opt1: "Woe unto the inhabitants of the earth! for the great trumpet hath sounded, and the wrath of God is poured out"
opt2: "Behold the day of vengeance! for the sun is darkened, and the sword of the Almighty shall devour all flesh"
opt3: "Alas for the day! for the day of the LORD is at hand, and as a destruction from the Almighty shall it come"
opt4: "Cry aloud, O Zion! for the year of recompence is arrived, and none shall escape the fire of His jealousy"
correct: "Alas for the day! for the day of the LORD is at hand, and as a destruction from the Almighty shall it come"
explanation: Joel 1:15 (KJV) - "Alas for the day! for the day of the LORD is at hand, and as a destruction from the Almighty shall it come."

question: According to Joel 1:16-17, what condition overtook the seeds beneath the soil and the agricultural storage facilities?
opt1: The harvest was devoured by worms; the cisterns were shattered, and the granaries burned by foreign raiders
opt2: The wheat sprouted prematurely; the stone storehouses were emptied by famine, and the cellars filled with mire
opt3: The barley decayed in the ear; the threshing floors were deserted, and the winepresses broken in pieces
opt4: Meat, joy, and gladness are cut off from the house of God; the seed is rotten under their clods, the garners are laid desolate, and the barns are broken down, for the corn is withered
correct: Meat, joy, and gladness are cut off from the house of God; the seed is rotten under their clods, the garners are laid desolate, and the barns are broken down, for the corn is withered
explanation: Joel 1:16-17 (KJV) - "Is not the meat cut off before our eyes, yea, joy and gladness from the house of our God? The seed is rotten under their clods, the garners are laid desolate, the barns are broken down; for the corn is withered."

question: In Joel 1:18, how do the domestic cattle and flocks of sheep respond to the total absence of green pasture?
opt1: The beasts groan, the herds of cattle are perplexed because they have no pasture, and the flocks of sheep are made desolate
opt2: The cattle wander into the cities crying aloud, and the sheep perish upon the rocky crags of the mountains
opt3: The oxen fall in their stalls, and the rams butt one another in fury because of the parched ground
opt4: The herds flee toward the river Jordan, and the lambs are devoured by the lions of the wilderness
correct: The beasts groan, the herds of cattle are perplexed because they have no pasture, and the flocks of sheep are made desolate
explanation: Joel 1:18 (KJV) - "How do the beasts groan! the herds of cattle are perplexed, because they have no pasture; yea, the flocks of sheep are made desolate."

question: According to Joel 1:19-20, what prayer does Joel cry unto the LORD, and why do the beasts of the field cry unto God also?
opt1: "Hear my voice, O God of Jacob: for a drought hath consumed the vineyards, and the fountains are stopped with dust"
opt2: "O LORD, to thee will I cry: for the fire hath devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame hath burned all the trees of the field. The beasts of the field cry also unto thee: for the rivers of waters are dried up"
opt3: "Turn thine anger, O Holy One: for the locusts have stripped the hills, and the wild beasts roar in hunger"
opt4: "Look upon our affliction, O King of Zion: for the earth is burned like an oven, and the cattle languish without dew"
correct: "O LORD, to thee will I cry: for the fire hath devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame hath burned all the trees of the field. The beasts of the field cry also unto thee: for the rivers of waters are dried up"
explanation: Joel 1:19-20 (KJV) - "O LORD, to thee will I cry: for the fire hath devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame hath burned all the trees of the field. The beasts of the field cry also unto thee: for the rivers of waters are dried up, and the fire hath devoured the pastures of the wilderness."

question: In Joel 2:1-2, where is the alarm trumpet commanded to be blown, and how is the approaching Day of the LORD described in its darkness and uniqueness?
opt1: Sound the shofar at the gates of Jerusalem; a day of fire, brimstone, whirlwind, and smoke, as the lightning over Lebanon: an army of giants unlike any since the deluge
opt2: Blow the trumpet in Zion, sound an alarm in His holy mountain; a day of darkness, gloominess, clouds, and thick darkness, as the morning spread upon the mountains: a great people and strong, there hath not been ever the like, neither shall be any more after it
opt3: Blow the horn in the valley of Hinnom; a day of wrath, vengeance, trembling, and blood, as the storm over Carmel: horsemen of iron whose numbers exceed the sand
opt4: Sound the trumpet in Bethel and Gilgal; a day of mourning, famine, pestilence, and desolation: an empire of locusts whose noise shakes the earth
correct: Blow the trumpet in Zion, sound an alarm in His holy mountain; a day of darkness, gloominess, clouds, and thick darkness, as the morning spread upon the mountains: a great people and strong, there hath not been ever the like, neither shall be any more after it
explanation: Joel 2:1-2 (KJV) - "Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain: let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: for the day of the LORD cometh, for it is nigh at hand; A day of darkness and of gloominess, a day of clouds and of thick darkness, as the morning spread upon the mountains: a great people and a strong; there hath not been ever the like, neither shall be any more after it, even to the years of many generations."

question: According to Joel 2:3, what striking environmental contrast precedes and follows the devastating advance of this army?
opt1: "A whirlwind sweepeth before them; and behind them an earthquake shattereth: the land is as fertile Sharon before them, and behind them a sea of salt"
opt2: "Hail and brimstone fall before them; and behind them thick smoke riseth: the land is as green Carmel before them, and behind them ashes of grief"
opt3: "A fire devoureth before them; and behind them a flame burneth: the land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness; yea, and nothing shall escape them"
opt4: "Darkness marcheth before them; and behind them pestilence followeth: the land is as a fruitful orchard before them, and behind them parched sand"
correct: "A fire devoureth before them; and behind them a flame burneth: the land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness; yea, and nothing shall escape them"
explanation: Joel 2:3 (KJV) - "A fire devoureth before them; and behind them a flame burneth: the land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness; yea, and nothing shall escape them."

question: In Joel 2:4-6, how are the appearance, agility, and sound of the invading swarm described, and what physical reaction grips the people?
opt1: Appearance of winged lions tearing prey; roaring like the waves of the sea; before them the mighty men tremble and drop their weapons
opt2: Appearance of iron chariots driven by giants; clashing like shields in battle; before them the kings of the earth flee in terror
opt3: Appearance of fiery serpents flying through the air; hissing like furnaces; before them all knees become as water
opt4: Appearance of horses and horsemen running; leaping like the noise of chariots on mountain tops and flame devouring stubble; before their face people are much pained, and all faces gather blackness
correct: Appearance of horses and horsemen running; leaping like the noise of chariots on mountain tops and flame devouring stubble; before their face people are much pained, and all faces gather blackness
explanation: Joel 2:4-6 (KJV) - "The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses; and as horsemen, so shall they run. Like the noise of chariots on the tops of mountains shall they leap, like the noise of a flame of fire that devoureth the stubble, as a strong people set in battle array. Before their face the people shall be much pained: all faces shall gather blackness."

question: According to Joel 2:7-9, what unbroken military precision and urban penetration characterize the march of this host?
opt1: They run like mighty men, climb the wall like men of war, march every one on his ways and not break ranks; none thrusts another, they fall on the sword unwounded, run upon the wall, climb houses, and enter windows like a thief
opt2: They batter the gates with iron rams, tunnel beneath the foundations, and breach the towers; slaying the watchmen and burning the palaces
opt3: They surround the city with siege mounts, cut off the water of Gihon, and shoot arrows into the temple court without missing a mark
opt4: They leap over the battlements like leopards, crush the bronze bars of the gates, and plunder the gold vessels of the sanctuary
correct: They run like mighty men, climb the wall like men of war, march every one on his ways and not break ranks; none thrusts another, they fall on the sword unwounded, run upon the wall, climb houses, and enter windows like a thief
explanation: Joel 2:7-9 (KJV) - "They shall run like mighty men; they shall climb the wall like men of war; and they shall march every one on his ways, and they shall not break their ranks: Neither shall one thrust another; they shall walk every one in his path: and when they fall upon the sword, they shall not be wounded. They shall run to and fro in the city; they shall run upon the wall, they shall climb up upon the houses; they shall enter in at the windows like a thief."

question: In Joel 2:10-11, what cosmic convulsions accompany their march, and who leads this mighty army as its supreme commander?
opt1: The mountains melt like wax, the sea roars; the archangel Michael leads the host with a flaming sword against the rebellious nations
opt2: The earth quakes, heavens tremble, sun and moon are dark, stars withdraw shining; the LORD shall utter His voice before His army: for His camp is very great, strong that executeth His word, day of the LORD great and very terrible
opt3: The foundations of the hills shake, the skies rain blood; the king of Assyria marches at the head of seven hundred thousand horsemen
opt4: The stars fall like untimely figs, the heavens are rolled up; the angel of the bottomless pit leads the army of scorpions
correct: The earth quakes, heavens tremble, sun and moon are dark, stars withdraw shining; the LORD shall utter His voice before His army: for His camp is very great, strong that executeth His word, day of the LORD great and very terrible
explanation: Joel 2:10-11 (KJV) - "The earth shall quake before them; the heavens shall tremble: the sun and the moon shall be dark, and the stars shall withdraw their shining: And the LORD shall utter his voice before his army: for his camp is very great: for he is strong that executeth his word: for the day of the LORD is great and very terrible; and who can abide it?"

question: What internal, sincere repentance does the LORD demand in Joel 2:12-13, and what divine attributes of grace are highlighted?
opt1: "offer a thousand rams upon Mount Zion, and put on sackcloth of hair: for the LORD is righteous, unyielding in judgment, and pure in all His ways"
opt2: "proclaim a fast of forty days, and wash your hands in water: for the Almighty is fearful in praises, doing wonders among the children of men"
opt3: "turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning: And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil"
opt4: "fall upon your faces before the ark, and weep before the priests: for He is a consuming fire, jealous for His holy covenant"
correct: "turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning: And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil"
explanation: Joel 2:12-13 (KJV) - "Therefore also now, saith the LORD, turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning: And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil."

question: According to Joel 2:15-17, who is gathered for the solemn assembly, and what exact intercession are the priests to pray between the porch and the altar?
opt1: Assemble soldiers, captains, and princes; priests offer two lambs and say, "Avenge thy holy sanctuary upon the uncircumcised, and make Jerusalem a praise in the earth"
opt2: Gather the twelve tribal heads; Levites chant psalms and say, "Remember the oath sworn unto David, and break the yoke of the northern oppressor"
opt3: Assemble the entire congregation with fastings; high priest wears the breastplate and says, "Forgive the sins of our fathers, and restore the glory of the temple"
opt4: Gather people, elders, children, nursing infants; bridegroom out of chamber and bride out of closet; priests weep and say, "Spare thy people, O LORD, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?"
correct: Gather people, elders, children, nursing infants; bridegroom out of chamber and bride out of closet; priests weep and say, "Spare thy people, O LORD, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?"
explanation: Joel 2:15-17 (KJV) - "Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children, and those that suck the breasts: let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet. Let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O LORD, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?"

question: In Joel 2:18-20, how does the LORD respond to national repentance, what blessings are restored, and where is the northern army driven?
opt1: The LORD will be jealous for His land and pity His people; send corn, wine, and oil to satisfy them; remove far off the northern army into a barren and desolate land, with his face toward the east sea and hinder part toward the utmost sea, his stink coming up
opt2: The LORD will send twelve legions of angels; rebuild the fallen walls of Zion; drown the northern invaders in the river Euphrates, casting their armor into the sea
opt3: The LORD will establish perpetual peace; shower the land with gold and silver; consume the northern host with heavenly fire, leaving no remnant alive
opt4: The LORD will pour down sweet rain; multiply the flocks of sheep and herds of cattle; banish the invading army into the deserts of Egypt
correct: The LORD will be jealous for His land and pity His people; send corn, wine, and oil to satisfy them; remove far off the northern army into a barren and desolate land, with his face toward the east sea and hinder part toward the utmost sea, his stink coming up
explanation: Joel 2:18-20 (KJV) - "Then will the LORD be jealous for his land, and pity his people. Yea, the LORD will answer and say unto his people, Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil, and ye shall be satisfied therewith: and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen: But I will remove far off from you the northern army, and will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea, and his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up, because he hath done great things."

question: According to Joel 2:23-25, what climatic and agricultural restoration is promised to Zion, and what wasted years will God restore?
opt1: He will send dew upon the grass every morning; the olive trees will yield double fruit; and restore the seventy years of Babylonian desolation
opt2: He will cause the former rain and latter rain to come down in the first month; floors full of wheat, vats overflowing with wine and oil; and restore the years that the locust, cankerworm, caterpiller, and palmerworm have eaten
opt3: He will open the windows of heaven with gentle showers; the vineyards will bloom on every hill; and restore the forty years of wilderness wandering
opt4: He will water the land with springs from the sanctuary; the barns will be filled with fine flour; and restore the seven years of drought
correct: He will cause the former rain and latter rain to come down in the first month; floors full of wheat, vats overflowing with wine and oil; and restore the years that the locust, cankerworm, caterpiller, and palmerworm have eaten
explanation: Joel 2:23-25 (KJV) - "Be glad then, ye children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD your God: for he hath given you the former rain moderately, and he will cause to come down for you the rain, the former rain, and the latter rain in the first month. And the floors shall be full of wheat, and the vats shall overflow with wine and oil. And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpiller, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you."

question: In Joel 2:28-32, what landmark Pentecostal outpouring of the Spirit, cosmic wonders, and promise of universal salvation are prophesied for the latter days?
opt1: God will send the prophet Elijah to restore all things: priests shall speak with new tongues; the stars shall fall into the sea; and whosoever keepeth the Sabbath shall be saved
opt2: God will write His law upon the hearts of the princes: elders shall interpret nocturnal dreams; lightning shall burn the mountains; and whosoever offereth pure bullocks shall live
opt3: God will pour out His Spirit upon all flesh: sons and daughters shall prophesy, old men dream dreams, young men see visions; blood, fire, pillars of smoke; sun turned into darkness, moon into blood; and whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered
opt4: God will establish a new covenant with the house of David: prophets shall multiply throughout the earth; a great rainbow shall encompass Jerusalem; and circumcision shall triumph
correct: God will pour out His Spirit upon all flesh: sons and daughters shall prophesy, old men dream dreams, young men see visions; blood, fire, pillars of smoke; sun turned into darkness, moon into blood; and whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered
explanation: Joel 2:28, 30-32 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions ... And I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the LORD come. And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the LORD hath said, and in the remnant whom the LORD shall call."

question: In Joel 3:1-2, when the LORD brings again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, where will He gather all nations, and on what grounds will He plead with them?
opt1: In the valley of Hinnom; to punish them for burning children unto Molech and desecrating the sacred vessels
opt2: In the plains of Megiddo; to execute vengeance upon the kings of the earth who allied against the house of David
opt3: On the Mount of Olives; to divide the spoils of the Gentiles and restore the twelve tribal boundaries
opt4: In the valley of Jehoshaphat; to plead with them for His people and heritage Israel, whom they scattered among the nations, and parted His land
correct: In the valley of Jehoshaphat; to plead with them for His people and heritage Israel, whom they scattered among the nations, and parted His land
explanation: Joel 3:1-2 (KJV) - "For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land."

question: According to Joel 3:3, what callous human trafficking and casting of lots did the heathen nations commit against the captive children of Israel?
opt1: "And they have cast lots for my people; and have given a boy for an harlot, and sold a girl for wine, that they might drink"
opt2: "They have weighed my princes for silver; and have bartered young men for horses, and maidens for flagons of oil"
opt3: "They have enslaved my daughters in the palaces of Babylon; and have exchanged youths for iron swords and purple garments"
opt4: "They have branded my children with the marks of idols; and sold orphans for a measure of barley and a pair of shoes"
correct: "And they have cast lots for my people; and have given a boy for an harlot, and sold a girl for wine, that they might drink"
explanation: Joel 3:3 (KJV) - "And they have cast lots for my people; and have given a boy for an harlot, and sold a girl for wine, that they might drink."

question: In Joel 3:4-6, what indictment does the LORD bring against Tyre, Zidon, and Palestine, and to whom did they sell the children of Judah and Jerusalem?
opt1: They plundered the bronze sea of Solomon; and sold the Judahite exiles to the merchants of Tarshish for tin and lead
opt2: They took His silver, gold, and goodly pleasant things into their temples; and sold the children of Judah and Jerusalem unto the Grecians, to remove them far from their border
opt3: They burned the gates of the temple; and traded the daughters of Zion to the princes of Egypt for royal chariots
opt4: They confiscated the sacred priestly garments; and marched the Hebrew captives unto the satraps of Media
correct: They took His silver, gold, and goodly pleasant things into their temples; and sold the children of Judah and Jerusalem unto the Grecians, to remove them far from their border
explanation: Joel 3:5-6 (KJV) - "Because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things: The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border."

question: According to Joel 3:7-8, what divine recompence will God execute upon these slave trading nations, and to whom will their own sons and daughters be sold?
opt1: God will destroy the merchant fleets of Tyre; and deliver their princes into the hands of Babylon to labor in copper mines
opt2: God will burn the coastal cities with fire; and sell their children unto the desert nomads of Midian and Kedar
opt3: God will raise His people out of where they were sold, return recompence upon their own head, and sell their sons and daughters into the hand of Judah, who shall sell them to the Sabeans, to a people far off
opt4: God will drown their sailors in the Great Sea; and disperse their daughters among the islands of Chittim forever
correct: God will raise His people out of where they were sold, return recompence upon their own head, and sell their sons and daughters into the hand of Judah, who shall sell them to the Sabeans, to a people far off
explanation: Joel 3:7-8 (KJV) - "Behold, I will raise them out of the place whither ye have sold them, and will return your recompence upon your own head: And I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, to a people far off: for the LORD hath spoken it."

question: What famous paradoxical summons to apocalyptic warfare is proclaimed among the Gentiles in Joel 3:9-10?
opt1: "Beat your swords into plowshares, and your spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither learn war any more"
opt2: "Sound the war horn among the nations; assemble your iron chariots: let the kings of the earth take counsel against the LORD and His Anointed"
opt3: "Cast away your sickles and burn your grain; gird on armour of brass: let the young men boast of their strength before the gates of Zion"
opt4: "Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near; let them come up: Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong"
correct: "Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near; let them come up: Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong"
explanation: Joel 3:9-10 (KJV) - "Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near; let them come up: Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong."

question: According to Joel 3:11-12, why are the heathen summoned to awaken and march down into the valley of Jehoshaphat?
opt1: "for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about"; and Joel prays, "thither cause thy mighty ones to come down, O LORD"
opt2: "for there will I divide the royal inheritance among the twelve tribes of Israel in the presence of their enemies"
opt3: "for there shall the archangel Michael execute vengeance with the sword of justice upon all idolaters"
opt4: "for there shall the fire of heaven fall upon the armies of Gog and Magog to consume them without a remnant"
correct: "for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about"; and Joel prays, "thither cause thy mighty ones to come down, O LORD"
explanation: Joel 3:11-12 (KJV) - "Assemble yourselves, and come, all ye heathen, and gather yourselves together round about: thither cause thy mighty ones to come down, O LORD. Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about."

question: In Joel 3:13, under what double agricultural metaphor of ripe grain and bursting winepress is the execution of divine judgment depicted?
opt1: "Thresh the wheat with an iron flail, for the chaff must be burned: tread the olive press, for the oil of fury is filled"
opt2: "Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you down; for the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness is great"
opt3: "Cast the net into the deep, for the fish of iniquity are multiplied: gather the grapes of wrath, for the vintage is complete"
opt4: "Pluck up the tares and bind them in bundles for the fire: draw the wine of astonishment, for the cup of trembling is full"
correct: "Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you down; for the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness is great"
explanation: Joel 3:13 (KJV) - "Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you down; for the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness is great."

question: According to Joel 3:14-16, what multitudes assemble in what valley, and what cosmic refuge is the LORD for His people when He roars out of Zion?
opt1: Nations gathered in the valley of Megiddo; stars falling like meteors; the LORD shall descend upon the Mount of Olives; and He shall be a wall of fire around Jerusalem
opt2: All kings assembled in the valley of Shinar; earth melting with fervent heat; the LORD shall blow the seventh trumpet; and He shall give white robes to the martyrs
opt3: Multitudes in the valley of decision; sun and moon darkened; the LORD shall roar out of Zion and utter His voice from Jerusalem, heavens and earth shaking; but the LORD will be the hope of His people, and the strength of the children of Israel
opt4: Armies encamped in the valley of Jezreel; sky rolled back as a scroll; the LORD shall send His destroying angel; and He shall reign upon Mount Zion
correct: Multitudes in the valley of decision; sun and moon darkened; the LORD shall roar out of Zion and utter His voice from Jerusalem, heavens and earth shaking; but the LORD will be the hope of His people, and the strength of the children of Israel
explanation: Joel 3:14-16 (KJV) - "Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision. The sun and the moon shall be darkened, and the stars shall withdraw their shining. The LORD also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shall shake: but the LORD will be the hope of his people, and the strength of the children of Israel."

question: In Joel 3:17-18, how is holy Jerusalem preserved from foreign desecration, and what miraculous river of life will flow from the house of the LORD?
opt1: Jerusalem shall be encompassed with walls of jasper; twelve gates of pearl shall be opened; a river of pure crystal shall flow eastward into the Dead Sea
opt2: Jerusalem shall be crowned with the Shekinah glory; the heathen shall bring tribute daily; four rivers of Eden shall branch from under the bronze altar
opt3: Jerusalem shall be exalted above the hills; the ark of the covenant shall be revealed; living streams shall sweeten the wilderness of Judea
opt4: Jerusalem shall be holy, no strangers shall pass through her any more; mountains shall drop down new wine, hills flow with milk, rivers of Judah flow with waters, and a fountain shall come forth of the house of the LORD, watering the valley of Shittim
correct: Jerusalem shall be holy, no strangers shall pass through her any more; mountains shall drop down new wine, hills flow with milk, rivers of Judah flow with waters, and a fountain shall come forth of the house of the LORD, watering the valley of Shittim
explanation: Joel 3:17-18 (KJV) - "So shall ye know that I am the LORD your God dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain: then shall Jerusalem be holy, and there shall no strangers pass through her any more. And it shall come to pass in that day, that the mountains shall drop down new wine, and the hills shall flow with milk, and all the rivers of Judah shall flow with waters, and a fountain shall come forth of the house of the LORD, and shall water the valley of Shittim."

question: According to Joel 3:19-21, what desolation will befall Egypt and Edom, and what eternal dwelling place of the LORD concludes the prophecy?
opt1: Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom a desolate wilderness, for violence against Judah, shedding innocent blood; but Judah shall dwell for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation: for the LORD dwelleth in Zion
opt2: Egypt shall be submerged by the Red Sea, and Edom consumed by fire from Mount Paran; while Zion shall govern the nations: for the LORD is our King
opt3: Egypt shall be plundered by Assyria, and Edom become a den of jackals; while the children of Israel shall multiply as sand: for the LORD is Holy
opt4: Egypt shall be divided among four generals, and Edom trampled under foot; while the seed of David shall endure like the sun: for the LORD reigns
correct: Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom a desolate wilderness, for violence against Judah, shedding innocent blood; but Judah shall dwell for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation: for the LORD dwelleth in Zion
explanation: Joel 3:19-21 (KJV) - "Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom shall be a desolate wilderness, for the violence against the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land. But Judah shall dwell for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation. For I will cleanse their blood that I have not cleansed: for the LORD dwelleth in Zion."
